one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely concerning experience — serious safety issue!!

I brought both my daughter and my son to a semi-private swimming lessons yesterday (Aug 29) at noon for the first time, and what happened was extremely upsetting and unacceptable.
I was initially told that because of my son’s age (2 y.o.), I was required to be in the water with him. However, immediately before the lesson, the instructor confidently told me that I did not need to be in the water because he would be able to supervise and manage both children. I trusted that assurance.
While the instructor was teaching my daughter (4 y.o.), he was not keeping his eyes on my son. My son then decided to go in the water. I watched in horror as my son remained underwater for what felt like at least 10 seconds, while the instructor did not notice.
What was even more alarming was that the first-aid employee approached the instructor slowly and asked about my son before the instructor realized that my son was underwater. The instructor then picked my son up and placed him back on the bench.
As a parent, I cannot adequately describe how terrifying it was to watch my child underwater and realize that the person responsible for supervising him had no idea what was happening. I was absolutely furious and came very close to confronting the staff immediately. I chose to remain calm and allowed the lesson to resume once my son had been settled.
This was not a minor oversight. A child was underwater for several seconds without the instructor noticing.
I am extremely disappointed and angry about what happened, especially after the instructor specifically assured me that I did not need to be in the water because he could safely supervise both children. After the lesson, I asked the instructor what happened, he said he didn’t see my son go in the water but he was fine because he was holding his breath. I asked how he could tell that my son was holding his breath… the response was because he wasn’t coughing when he came out of the water. I didn’t feel like talking to them at this point. I tried not to overreact because my son is fine. However, the facility needs to review its supervision and safety procedures so that another parent does not have to experience what I experienced.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve been going to Montreal Pickleball on a regular basis, at least 3–4 times a month, either through open play or through court reservations. I've also taken a few lessons at the club. My experiences have, for the most part, been very pleasant.

Unfortunately, I recently had a couple of experiences that left a very sour taste in my mouth.  It's been made very clear that customer loyalty and common sense don’t seem to mean much here.

A few weeks ago, I had to cancel an open play because of a tornado warning. I asked if they could provide a credit for the session. They refused, despite the fact that there were 40+ people at the open play. I wasn’t asking for a refund because I simply changed my mind, I was dealing with a legitimate safety situation. A little customer service and flexibility would have gone a long way.

Today, I made an honest mistake when booking a court. I thought I had booked 11:00–1:00, but I had actually booked 10:30–12:30. When I arrived at 11:00, the part owner working the desk said "you're late". It was pretty obvious I had made a mistake when booking. He said he would do me a favor and not charge me from 10:30 and let me play from 11:00–1:00. While that was appreciated, the interaction still left me feeling like I was being treated as though I was trying to get away with something.

There were plenty of empty courts, so this could have simply been treated as an honest mistake. Instead, I felt like I was shamed. The owner wasn’t openly rude, but his attitude communicated very clearly that he wasn’t particularly interested in keeping my business.

And that’s the biggest problem: I’ve been a regular customer. I’ve spent money there repeatedly. I’ve taken lessons. I’ve supported the business. You would think that would earn at least a little goodwill when a customer makes an honest mistake or encounters an unusual situation.

Instead, the overall attitude seems to be: follow the rules exactly, or you’re on your own.
Businesses absolutely need policies, but there is also something called customer service. Loyal customers should not be made to feel like criminals or like they’re trying to take advantage of the business.

Come 1 o'clock, we were midgame and decided we wanted to finish . We were the only people in the entire club other than the staff. We figured we would just pay for the extra time on our way out. The owner made it a point to come over and tell us our time was up. Again, he made us feel like we were taking advantage of the business.  If it were my club, I would have waited at the desk for the customers to pay on their way out. Or better yet, since the club was completely empty, I probably would have not charged for the extra 20 or 25 mins to finish the game.

When we tried to voice our concerns, his energy was giving he couldn't care less. He asked my friend if a free Gatorade would make her feel better.

After today, I won’t be going back. It's unfortunate because the coaches and people I have met here through open play have been great but I would rather bring my business to a club that actually makes customers feel welcome and valued.

Very Disappointing Experience at Aroma Spa

Unfortunately, our experience at Aroma Spa was extremely disappointing. My husband had booked an hour-long massage for my daughter and me. When we arrived, I explained to the spa front desk that I have been experiencing significant back and neck pain following two recent car accidents and that I am currently doing physiotherapy back home. I asked if it would be possible to reduce my massage to 30 minutes instead of the full hour.

Rather than showing any understanding or consideration for my situation, I was told that I would be charged a cancellation fee if I shortened the appointment. I found this extremely disappointing. It felt as though the priority was simply the money rather than the customer’s circumstances or well-being.

What made the experience even more frustrating is that, after paying for the massage, you are still expected to tip the staff member who provides the service.

I am still at the hotel and would be happy to give Aroma Spa an opportunity to make this right. I believe customer service is not just about policies, it is also about compassion, understanding, and how you treat your guests when unexpected circumstances arise.

If someone from Aroma Spa reaches out and resolves this matter to my satisfaction, I would be more than happy to update my review accordingly. I sincerely hope they do. Please reply to this review and I will connect with you.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m a regular customer at this location and usually come here once or twice a week. I’ve actually liked this Wendy’s, which makes today’s experience especially disappointing.
Today, I placed two separate orders through the self-service kiosk using the same credit card. Both orders appeared to go through successfully, and order numbers were displayed on the screen. My first order came out, but my second order never did.
I waited for a long time while many customers who had ordered after me received their food. Eventually, I went to the counter to ask about my order. The manager’s initial response was extremely rude and dismissive. I was essentially told that my order had never been placed, as if I had simply made it up.
Since the kiosk does not provide a printed receipt, I had no physical proof of the order. I had to call my partner, who had already gone home, and have him come back to show the credit card transaction on his banking app. The transaction clearly showed two Wendy’s purchases, confirming that both orders had in fact gone through.
Only then did they make my food.
What upset me the most was not the possibility of a technical issue. Mistakes and technical problems can happen. What was unacceptable was the way the manager treated me from the moment I asked about my missing order. There was no attempt to politely investigate the situation, no acknowledgment that I had been waiting for a long time, and not even a simple “I’m sorry” after it was confirmed that I had actually paid for the order.
Even when my food was finally handed to me, there was still no apology or explanation whatsoever. The attitude was essentially, “Here’s your burger,” as though I were the one who had caused the problem.
Good customer service is not about never making mistakes. It is about how you treat customers when something goes wrong. Unfortunately, this manager showed no sense of accountability or concern for the customer experience.
I’m particularly disappointed because I used to like this location and was a regular customer. Unfortunately, as long as this manager is working here, I will not be coming back.

Very disappointing and concerning behaviour from a marketing firm that claims to support local and small businesses.

They have taken content created by small businesses and other marketing professionals, removed watermarks, and used that work without permission. That is not supporting the local business community. It is taking advantage of the creativity, time, and investment of the very businesses a marketing firm should be helping.

There is a major difference between sharing someone’s work with proper credit and taking it, stripping away the creator’s watermark, and presenting it as your own. For a marketing company, there should be an even higher standard of respect for intellectual property and the work behind a brand.

If you are a small business considering hiring this company, I would strongly recommend looking closely at how they conduct their own marketing before trusting them with yours.

Very, very average food, dishes were hit or miss, decent decor but disgustingly unclean  washrooms.  Birthday dinner plans. Booked a table for 4. We chose this restaurant based upon the multiple reviews saying it was the best Indian food ever. The experience was very poor. Read on.  When we walked in, there were two tables occupied. As it was a birthday, they had put balloons and a Happy Birthday banner at our table, which seemed a good start but things started unraveling later. The server cum hostess Sanmeet was very nice, despite being the only person we saw, she was  efficient. We ordered Pickleback shots to start. Ordered the butter chicken nachos, peri peri dumplings, Chicken gilafi kabab. The dumplings were definitely very good. The nacho chips were stale and crushed as if the dregs of a bag had been layered on a plate. The butter chicken was decent but the experience ruined by old nachos chips. The Gilafi kabab reeked of overly of garlic. Most average in taste. Those who have had delicately spiced, soft seekh kababs will understand. Anyway, we then decided not to continue with mains, and moved on elsewhere.

On the washrooms - they were poorly maintained with no soap in the ladies, and our group said the men’s was disgusting  and reeked of urine. In the ladies, there was a bad leak from the roof, right where one stood to wash hands, so water dripping on your head and a puddle in the floor. The server said it’s an old house so, during inclement weather, leaks happen.  The toilets were stained and dirty.

one_star_reviews.text:
My Disappointing Experience with NRI Marriage Bureau – Please Be Careful Before Paying

I submitted my matrimonial advertisement to NRI Marriage Bureau on October 11 and clearly explained the type of matches I was looking for. Unfortunately, my experience with their service has been extremely disappointing.

Despite giving them clear instructions, they repeatedly sent me profiles that did not match my requirements. I also received photos of men who appeared to be married, which raised serious concerns for me about the accuracy and verification of the profiles being shared. At times, they would send several photos and later blame me for not answering calls, rather than properly addressing my concerns.

After I complained, a person named Gurpreet Singh Taliwal contacted me and apologized, promising that they would be more careful and provide better-matched profiles going forward. Nimrat Kaur was also handling my case. I explained my concerns to her in detail, but I did not feel that my concerns were taken seriously or that the service improved.

A matrimonial service should give people hope and confidence, not leave them feeling discouraged, disrespected, and emotionally drained. Comments and interactions that make clients feel as though nobody likes them or wants to marry them can seriously affect their confidence and self-esteem. Marriage is already an emotional and personal matter, and clients deserve to be treated with dignity, sensitivity, and respect.

Eventually, I told them that if they could not find suitable matches, they should stop sending me profiles. I specifically asked them not to send me unsuitable or potentially inaccurate profiles and requested a refund of the CAD $450 I had paid. However, they refused to refund my money. I was also told, in effect, that they were not afraid of court cases or negative reviews and that people like me could post reviews without affecting their business.

I find this attitude extremely disappointing. Customers who pay for a service deserve professional communication, honest information, and fair treatment. If a business cannot provide the service promised, it should at least address complaints responsibly and consider a fair resolution.

I am requesting that the management of NRI Marriage Bureau review how its staff handle clients, verify matrimonial profiles, and respond to complaints. Please ensure that clients are not misled, that their concerns are taken seriously, and that their money is handled fairly.

I also have concerns about the photographs shared with me, including whether they were current and whether the individuals had authorized their use. I believe the bureau should clarify how these photos are obtained, verified, and used. I intend to seek appropriate advice regarding my concerns and the options available to me.

My recommendation: Please do your research, ask clear questions about the service and refund policy, and obtain all terms in writing before paying any matrimonial bureau. Based on my personal experience, I would urge others to exercise caution before choosing this service.

I hope the management takes this complaint seriously and improves its service so that other people do not have to go through a similarly distressing experience

AVOID — MY EXPERIENCE FELT LIKE A SCAM. $330 WASTED AND NOT ONE FAMILY CONNECTION IN THREE MONTHS.

I purchased NRI Marriage Bureau’s services to find a match for my brother. Mr. Munish initially contacted me and quoted approximately $400. When I said it was too expensive, he spoke with his manager and returned with a reduced price of $330. The offer was tempting because I genuinely wanted to find a suitable rishta for my brother, so I paid despite having read several negative reviews. I regret ignoring those warnings.

After I paid, Paramjit Kaur was assigned as my consultant. During the entire three-month membership, they did not connect us with even one family. They only forwarded profiles, with a limit of three per week. Several profiles appeared inactive or uninterested, and it did not seem that the team confirmed each person’s current interest before sending their information. Forwarding random profiles is not the same as arranging genuine, vetted introductions between families.

Our criteria were very open: no caste restriction, no city restriction and no relocation restriction. Considering this flexibility, I find it extremely disappointing that they could not arrange even one conversation with a family in three months.

After my experience, I also question the authenticity of some of the highly positive reviews because they do not reflect the service I received at all. I cannot confirm who wrote them, but I strongly recommend reading the critical reviews carefully instead of relying only on the overall rating.

Based on my personal experience, I would strongly advise others not to purchase these services. Please do not be tempted by a suddenly reduced price or pressured into paying quickly. $330 is a significant amount of money, and I received no meaningful introductions or results. My interactions were primarily with Mr. Munish and Paramjit Kaur. Please think carefully before paying NRI Marriage Bureau.
My opinion was positive, but I need to change my mind. I prefer to refrain from commenting.

one_star_reviews.text:
Have taken this course myself and had other friends take it. Their scoring system for the test is inconsistent and subjective. I've witnessed it multiple times where instructors are distracted and fail to give the signal to stop in time.

On my test they forgot to blow the whistle entirely. Fortunately I was able to stop in time due to exp, but ive seen countless others fail this way. Imagine asking a rider in training to make an emergency stop within 2.5' of the pylons.

I also watched them hand out perfect scores to those who knocked over pylons and made mistakes. They calculate your speed with a stopwatch and a visual on how far you traveled. The degree of accuracy using this method has a large margin of error.

The amount of stress I have seen this course put on people is absurd. Everyone worries the entire time they are going to lose their $650 due to their policy. At the end of the day your $ and training quality comes down to whichever way the instructor is feeling that day.

I also noticed a large disparity between the quality of the lead instructors. Sandros did a VERY good job, everyone passed his class. Zach had people falling off their bikes all day and half the class in a stir over them failing to take accountability for not giving the signal on time. You cant fail riders because you won't take accountability for your mistake, especially with no refund.

I wish I could give this 5 stars for the sake of Sandro and Ted, but unfortunately there is a lack of consistency with the other trainers that reflects poorly on this course as a whole. Do better

I strongly recommend that anyone considering this firm think very carefully before paying them any money.

I clearly explained what I expected from the representation before retaining the firm. After they had my money, I found myself arguing with counsel late at night by email about those same expectations, with him disputing what I had originally communicated. Had his position been made clear before I paid, I would never have retained him.

I paid $2,000, yet the firm never went on the record as my counsel. After I terminated the relationship, the firm retained the entire $2,000 and treated a $6,000 trial fee as payable, while characterizing the remaining $4,300 as a “discretionary fee write-off.” I dispute this because the signed retainer specifically provides for a $1,000 file-opening and preliminary-advice fee upon premature termination.

I am now stuck trying to recover the additional $1,000 that I dispute they are entitled to keep. I have formally demanded its return, and at this point it appears I may have to take the matter through the Alberta Court of King’s Bench fee-review process just to try to get my money back.

The entire experience has caused me to lose trust in this firm. I would not retain them again and would strongly caution others to document exactly what they are being promised and understand every fee provision before handing over any money.

one_star_reviews.text:
A Disquisition on Mediocrity: Breakfast at the Taylor location.

On the morning of Wednesday, 19 August 2026, we subjected ourselves to breakfast at the Taylor location. What followed was an exercise in the depressingly familiar: yet another interchangeable, franchise-template “pancake joint” of the Winnipeg variety, its every plate evidently provisioned by the same industrial commissary—SYSCO Food Services of Winnipeg—that supplies the city’s indistinguishable cohort of imitators.

I ordered the Eggs Benedict. The result was as predictable as it was uninspired: a study in institutional blandness. The so-called hollandaise arrived as that same pallid, flavourless yellow slurry one encounters at every other SYSCO-dependent establishment in the city—an emulsified non-entity that insults both the egg and the palate. The accompanying “home-style” hash browns proved equally anonymous: under-seasoned, textureless, and wholly devoid of the caramelised edge or herbal presence that might distinguish them from the identical specimen served anywhere else within the municipal radius. The English muffin, dry and unbuttered, completed the tableau of indifference.

As for the syrup: its aggressively artificial flavour continues to linger with a tenacity that borders on the punitive. One is left not merely disappointed, but actively working to expunge the chemical aftertaste.

Service was adequate in the most perfunctory sense—neither actively offensive nor in any way memorable. Nothing in the experience, however, supplies the slightest inducement to return. This is not cuisine; it is the efficient, corporate replication of the lowest common denominator, executed without ambition, imagination, or shame.

I am extremely disappointed by my experience at this store, particularly because I have had positive experiences with the brand in the past and have purchased multiple items from Loewe over the years.

I recently made a purchase of around $6000, which included a denim jacket and a pair of jeans. I had a perfectly pleasant shopping experience with my sales associate Michel and had no issues during the purchase itself.

After the transaction was completed, I was asked to sign one of the receipts. I did not think much of it and signed it.

After leaving the store, I purchased a Bottega Veneta denim jacket that I preferred, so I decided to return the Loewe jacket. I also decided to return the jeans because, after trying them with different tops at home, I realized the fit was not flattering. The jeans were not even the pair I had originally gone to the store for, as the pair I wanted was unavailable in store and I had planned to order them online.

When I returned to the store next day , the manager Pierre informed me that I could not receive a refund and would only be given store credit that could be used exclusively at the physical store. This restriction had not been communicated to me during the purchase.

When I explained this, rather than acknowledging that the policy had not been clearly communicated, I was told that “it was your responsibility as a customer to read what you are signing.” He then followed that by saying, “This is not like shopping at H&M.”

I found that comment deeply disrespectful and completely inappropriate. It came across as though I was being looked down upon as shopping at a more affordable retailer, which is particularly disappointing coming from a luxury brand.

I have considerable experience shopping with luxury brands and I completely understand that retailers may have specific return policies. That is not the issue. A store is entitled to establish whatever return policy it chooses, but customers should be made clearly aware of significant restrictions before completing a purchase and not after the transaction has been completed and the receipt has been printed and signed.

When you are spending over $6000 on two pieces of clothing, you are not only paying for the products. You are also paying for the level of service and communication that should come with a luxury shopping experience.

I subsequently raised the matter with customer service, and the store director Nattiya, reached out to me. I appreciate that she acknowledged that the H&M comment and Pierre’s behaviour were inappropriate and out of line.

Unfortunately, what was most disappointing was the lack of accountability at the time of the return. Instead of blaming me for not reading something I was asked to sign after the transaction had already been completed, I would have expected the store to acknowledge that the policy had not been adequately communicated and handle the situation with professionalism and courtesy.

This experience has unfortunately changed my perception of the brand. I have previously enjoyed shopping with Loewe, but after this interaction, I would not feel comfortable returning to the brand.

Luxury is not simply about the price of the product, it is also about how the customer is treated.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would strongly suggest thinking twice before working with this organization.

Just over 10 years ago, I set up an RESP for my son and life insurance for my wife and I through Investors Group. When I signed on, extensive promises were made about the ongoing advice and service we would receive. It has now been approximately six years since anyone from this company proactively contacted me.

Recently, our life insurance reached its 10 year renewal date and automatically renewed. Our premium went from approximately $70 per month to $270 per month, an increase of roughly 286%. I received no contact from Investors Group before this happened. Because the premiums were being withdrawn automatically, I didn't discover the increase until seven months later.

When I contacted Investors Group, I was told that Jess Patterson and Andrew Crowe were the advisors assigned to my account. Until I initiated contact, I had never heard from either of them. When we spoke, they apologized and acknowledged that I had essentially been lost in the system.

What makes the situation particularly frustrating is that they were then able to offer replacement life insurance for less than $100 per month, yet I was told nothing could be done about the seven months during which $270 per month had been withdrawn.

Think about that for a moment: my monthly insurance cost was allowed to automatically increase from approximately $70 to $270 without a single conversation with my assigned advisors, but once I discovered it and made a phone call, suddenly there was an option to bring my insurance cost back below $100 per month.

I understand there may be contractual language allowing the insurance company to automatically renew a term policy at predetermined rates. That isn't really the point of this review. I used Investors Group because I believed I was paying for professional financial advice and ongoing service — not simply the original transaction.

If an advisor is assigned to my family's accounts, I don't think expecting one conversation in six years, particularly before a major change like this, is an unreasonable expectation.

I'm sure there will be an explanation about policy terms, renewal notices, or which company was technically responsible for what. None of that changes my experience: Investors Group benefited from my business when these products were established, yet the ongoing service I was promised simply wasn't there when it mattered, and there has been no accountability.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Investors Group. There are plenty of other financial advisors and organizations competing for your business. I would strongly recommend considering them.

I had a very bad experience with Hina Mayani.

Hina's attitude was one of the most disappointing parts of my experience. Whenever I tried to ask questions about my own case, she was rude, dismissive, and unwilling to explain things properly. At times, her behaviour made me feel as though I had no right to question the service I was paying for. Clients deserve basic courtesy and respect, not arrogance. My application had a 30-day deadline for submitting additional information. I provided all the required documents during the first week, yet the submission was delayed until the last day, when I followed up. I had to call myself just to find out what was happening. This level of carelessness created unnecessary stress and demonstrated a serious lack of professionalism on the part of the consultant, Hina. The funny part is that she told me she is a lawyer, then later I found that she was actually a consultant. Ultimately, due to the lack of proper representation, my application was refused.

Before receiving payment, the responses were quick. Once the money was paid, getting a simple reply became a struggle. I had to send multiple follow-up emails and wait days just to receive basic updates. This was very unacceptable. It felt like I was important only until the payment was made.

one_star_reviews.text:
Do not stay here if you are tenting, or even expecting a quiet night in general. The campground is well maintained and clean, but there are severe shortcomings in operations. Read below:

Noise- quiet hours I think are 11pm, not the normal 10pm. They aren’t enforced. It’s also in the middle of town and the park, so other people who aren’t guests are around constantly. I dealt with some extremely bothersome RVers who were loud til 1-2am and kept everyone else nearby awake. More about that below.

Staff- It’s teenagers/young adults who are very nice and respectful. However, when I asked them about people being extremely loud into the night and deal with them, the staff wasn’t forceful enough to get the problem people to stop. I think it was an age issue, young people asking older (also likely drunk) adults to quiet down, which was unsuccessful.

People - again, the staff is nice and respectful, but certain guests were quite the opposite. Partying into the night, burning plastic instead of throwing away trash. It didn’t stop even asking staff to deal with it. That ruins it for the respectful guests.

Water- there isn’t any (if you are tenting). You are deliberately not given water. Reserves only for RVs. Same for electricity, even if you want to pay for an electric site. You have to ask for a handle/key and use an unoccupied site. They are reluctant to hand that out. Otherwise you fill in the bathrooms.

Light - it’s next to baseball fields, so there are huge floodlights that will also illuminate your spot. I think they got shut off around 1am. Impossible to sleep early.

Cleanliness- good. No dog droppings, no other animal droppings, bathrooms clean, showers clean.

Never sign a contract with this company.

Our family paid one full year of homestay fees in advance, but the company terminated our contract for reasons that we found completely unreasonable.

One of the reasons they gave for terminating our contract was that I had not responded to their email within two days — over a weekend. They used this as justification for ending the contract, even though they themselves do not respond to emails over the weekend. We found it extremely unreasonable that they expected us to respond within such a short timeframe, including the weekend, while they did not hold themselves to the same standard.

Because of the sudden termination and the way the situation was handled, we became seriously concerned about our child’s safety and living situation. We eventually had no choice but to arrange a different homestay ourselves.

Despite this, the company has still not returned approximately $6,000 that we paid in advance.

We are currently taking legal action to recover the money, but the issue remains unresolved and we have yet to receive our refund.

What is especially upsetting is that we originally trusted this company because it was recommended through a government-related website. We never expected to experience something like this from a company presented as a trustworthy homestay provider.

This situation has caused an enormous amount of stress for our entire family, both financially and emotionally. Based on our experience, I strongly recommend that other families carefully reconsider before signing any contract or paying large amounts of money in advance to this company.

​Save your time, money, and sanity: do not eat here. The service was trash, and the food was virtually inedible. The only redeeming part of the entire ordeal was the chutney—everything else was an absolute disaster.
​Absurd Wait Times & Terribly Careless Service: We waited a ridiculous 2.5 hours just to get our food. When we finally asked for normal tap water, our server didn't care in the slightest and brought us iced water instead. The staff was completely nonchalant, detached, and unbothered by the delays.
​Inedible, Poorly Prepared Food: We ordered two kulchas: an aloo paneer kulcha and a patty kulcha. Both were baked to an absolute crisp—extremely dry and so rock-hard it was practically impossible to chew or eat.
​Over-Spiced Chole: The chole served alongside was completely ruined. To be clear, it wasn't overly chili-spicy; it was loaded with an absurd, heavy-handed amount of raw, unbalanced spices that totally overwhelmed the dish, leaving zero actual flavor.
​Greedy Pricing & Bizarre Extra Charges: Majha Heights has already set extremely high, unjustifiable menu prices, but to make matters worse, this is the first restaurant in my life that actually charges extra money for an extra portion of chole with a kulcha. Expect to be nickel-and-dimed for basic meal components.
​Terrible Ambiance & Hygiene: The atmosphere inside is miserable. There is virtually zero lighting, the noise level is deafeningly high, and the floors were visibly dirty.
​From the incompetent front-of-house service to the dried-out, over-spiced food and dirty facility, Majha Heights Brampton fails on every single level. Hands down one of the worst food places I have ever visited in my entire life. Avoid at all costs!

one_star_reviews.text:
Richmond doesn't have many options for larger, comfortable furnished suites, and Level is genuinely one of the few choices in the area if that's what you're looking for. To be fair, the unit itself was nice — the furniture and appliances were new, and the location is convenient. But I don't think it was worth the price.

Check-in is self-service:an email the day before with no entry code, so I was locked outside the building on arrival and had to call for a long time to sort it out. Of the 3 fobs provided, one didn't work at all, and the other two didn't open the parkade — this took nearly two weeks to resolve, and in the meantime we had to get out of the car and dial an access code every time we entered the garage. There's also no proper check-in walkthrough — nobody tells you where to park, where to take out garbage, or how to access the pool/gym listed on their website. You have to ask for everything yourself; nothing is proactively explained.

The bigger issues:

Wifi was included in the rate but was spotty from day one and often didn't work at all. After reporting it, it took two weeks to get someone to look at it. We eventually paid out of pocket to install our own internet.

The building manager noticed our door lock battery was low during an unrelated visit and said it'd be replaced the next day — it wasn't. A few days later we came home to find the lock completely dead, locking our whole family out for about 2 hours.
One morning the freezer stopped working. We reported it immediately, were told someone would follow up, but heard nothing all day — a lot of food spoiled and no one has taken responsibility for it.

Nice unit, but the repeated maintenance failures and lack of basic support made this one of the most frustrating stays I've paid this much for.

Unfortunately, my experience with this lawyer Barakah Bello through Legal Aid was extremely disappointing. I did not feel that my best interests as her client were properly represented or prioritized.

Throughout my case, I felt there was a serious lack of communication, preparation, and advocacy. I often felt like I was left to figure things out on my own rather than having a lawyer who was actively looking out for me and protecting my interests.

What concerned me the most was how some interactions with the opposing lawyer were handled. From my perspective, it sometimes felt as though my concerns were not being taken seriously and that the approach being taken benefited the opposing side rather than me as the client.

I hired a lawyer because I needed someone to advocate for me, explain my options, and make sure my interests were protected. Instead, I was left feeling like I was paying for representation without actually receiving the support and advocacy I needed.

The situation became even more upsetting because, in my experience, important matters were not handled properly. There was an incident where the person I had a restraining order involving was able to physically push me while I was trying to enter the house. As a client, I expected my lawyer to take my safety and the legal protections in place extremely seriously.

This was an extremely stressful and important situation for me, and I left the experience feeling disappointed, unsupported, and let down. I personally did not feel that this lawyer was advocating for me or protecting my best interests.

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this lawyer or this firm to someone who needs strong, attentive, and client-focused legal representation.

I saw people still coming in to see the show homes, and honestly, it made me feel quite sad because it reminded me of how excited I was about buying a new home last year.

I also saw the most recent one-star review, and I completely understand what the person described. Many of the issues they mentioned are very similar to what we have personally experienced.

We also moved in in 2025, and we still have outstanding deficiencies. In our experience, communication from the builder has been very limited. The only time we found them to be particularly responsive was when we initially reported the deficiencies. Honestly, when I first moved in, I was so happy that I was considering leaving a five-star review.

Unfortunately, since then, there are still items that have not been addressed despite our repeated calls, texts, and emails. As time has gone on, we have also identified additional deficiencies that still need attention.

Before moving here, I had lived in two other homes built by different developers, and I had never experienced this level of ongoing deficiencies. Perhaps we are simply unlucky, but I remember researching negative reviews about the builder before purchasing and hoping that we would not have the same experience. Looking back, I wish I had paid more attention to those reviews.

We have experienced a number of workmanship issues, and at this point, we honestly aren't sure what else we can do to have the remaining deficiencies addressed.

I also noticed from the other one-star review that some people are considering legal action. I am actually considering what options available for me, but I have never discussed this with any of our neighbours, so it was surprising to see that others may be experiencing similar issues.I guess we are not alone in feeling this way.

My experience with G4U Security at the Bell Performing Arts Centre on October 2, 2026, raised serious concerns about the training and supervision of their security staff.

A situation involving people dancing should have been handled through clear communication and de-escalation. Instead, approximately 4–5 security staff became involved and unnecessarily physically handled us. Even after we complied and were peacefully walking down the stairs, we were pushed from behind, creating a serious risk of falling and injury.

When we asked to speak with the person responsible for the security team, we were denied that opportunity. A security staff member instead used profane and disrespectful language toward us and ordered us to leave. The shift supervisor also did not escalate our request to venue management.

I later personally spoke with a Bell Performing Arts Centre manager, who acknowledged issues with how the situation had been handled, including the number of security staff involved and management not being informed when we requested to speak with someone responsible.

Based on my experience, this raises serious concerns about staff training, de-escalation, communication, and on-site supervision. Professional security should use communication to resolve a situation when people are already complying, rather than escalating it into unnecessary physical contact.

From the moment we arrived, the doctor pressured us into making a decision. He said if didn't act now we'd have a tiny tiny chance of ever conceiving. He said that our chance to receive government funding would close if we didn't make a decision RIGHT NOW. SO.... we caved under his pressure...

Next thing you know, we're given mountains of paper information to sift through on our own about the process and drugs my wife will be taking with no guidance, verbal explanations or comforting reassurance.

Through the process of IVF, we were given some pretty intense drugs with some very serious side effects that we were to educate ourselves on. They just handed us a bunch of papers, abandoned us, gave us some syringes and we were all on our own. Any questions? Forget it. Nobody answers the phone. If you actually get through to somebody, you get attitude.

2 years after this terrible experience we went to a different fertility clinic. The experience couldn't be any more opposite than REPRO MED. They ended up giving us a different solution to IVF that was completely free. Turns out my wife had a mis-shaped uterus and a routine surgery resulted in IMMEDIATE natural conception. We are now blessed with our beautiful 2 year old.

GO ANYWHERE OTHER THAN HERE. PLEASE. IF IT'S NOT TOO LATE, TURN AROUND!!!

*Title: Major billing errors, unaddressed security issues, and terrible communication.*

Please think twice before committing to this clinic’s services. While undergoing fertility treatments here, I experienced serious issues with their front desk staff. Their poor communication and dismissive handling created unnecessary stress during an already difficult process.

Worse, their financial management is deeply concerning. The clinic completely mismanaged our billing, resulting in a massive medication overcharge. While the Director of Finance admitted to the overcharge in writing on June 3, 2025 and promised an $848 credit, their system failed to properly account for it.

To make matters worse, I also alerted the clinic that my bank flagged a major security vulnerability where payments sent to their official email were being maliciously intercepted. The clinic entirely ignored this severe security alert and never followed up.

Now, over 14 months later, they have resurfaced demanding an uncorrected, inflated balance of over $1,600 while completely erasing the $848 credit they already acknowledged owing me. Their math does not add up, their delays are unacceptable, and their follow-up timing shows a lack of accountability.

Patients have a right to know about these hidden financial risks, sloppy accounting, and poor administrative practices before trusting this place with their care and money. Be very careful with your billing and medical records here.

I went to this Dollarama on Monday, August 31, at around 9:00 PM. My original purchase was around $25, and I had a $100 bill that I had just withdrawn from an ATM.
There was a woman working there who told me she was the manager, along with a male employee who was wearing glasses(he is a good guy I like him he is fast and respectful with me every time). I gave the $100 bill to the cashier, and the woman came over to check it. She told me they could not accept the $100 bill because there was a line.
I found this very confusing because I had just received the $100 bill from an ATM. I went back to the ATM and put the $100 bill back, and the ATM accepted it without any problem.
I then removed some of my items, bringing the total down to about $13. I gave her $15 and expected my change back. Instead of giving me my change, she was talking to someone on the phone while wearing white AirPods. I was standing there waiting for my change while she continued her phone conversation instead of finishing the transaction.
I understand that employees can be busy, but customers should still be treated respectfully and professionally. The way this situation was handled was frustrating and disappointing.
I honestly don’t understand who hired her, who trained her, or who gave her the manager position if this is how customers are treated. A manager should know how to communicate with customers properly and handle transactions professionally
I hope Dollarama looks into this situation and provides better customer service and management training.

Terrible experience at the King George Hub location. My twin sisters ordered TWO separate birthday rewards through two different Marble Slab app accounts. What should have been a quick pickup took almost AN HOUR because of constant confusion and back-and-forth with the employee, Gagan.

She had to contact the manager close to 10 times for basic issues, and even another employee eventually told her she had mixed up the orders.

After ALL that waiting, BOTH orders were still wrong. They ordered chocolate and mango but received chocolate and vanilla. They asked for almonds but got peanuts. They ordered waffle cones but received ice cream in cups with empty cones separately.

Even when my sister was already at the door leaving, Gagan called her back to scan again, despite that already being dealt with. My parents and one sister were waiting outside in the cold during all this.

My sisters are only visiting me and leave in four days, so this was supposed to be a nice birthday experience while they’re here. Instead, almost an hour of their evening was wasted and they still left with the wrong orders.

I’m not asking for a refund or anything free. Management simply needs to respect customers’ time and properly train employees before putting them in a front-facing position. I’ve genuinely never experienced something like this over two ice creams.

Everything was good except the strawberry topping. It tasted like it went bad. Other locations serve fresh strawberries so this was a bit shocking. I told the associate and she said it was refilled last night and kept in the freezer. I believe her, but it just tastes weird. So my suggestion was only made so she could try it out herself and make a note of it. Wasn't looking for a refund or exchange. Very disappointing experience.

I came in around 6:30 PM and ordered a Roasted Brown Sugar Pearl Milk Tea with 100% sugar and 100% ice. I understand it was later in the day and the store was very quiet, but that shouldn’t mean the quality of the drink or service should drop.

When I arrived, there was no one at the counter serving customers. The male employee was sitting down looking at his phone. After he came over to make my drink, I watched him pour the tea from a large container/bucket and prepare the drink without shaking it.

When I received it, the drink wasn’t cold at all, even though I specifically ordered 100% ice. I told him that the drink wasn’t cold, and his response was basically, “Wait for the ice to melt and it will get cold.”

That response honestly made no sense. I stood at the counter and shook the drink myself. The ice quickly melted, and the drink was STILL barely cold — it was almost like ordering a drink with no ice.

He then said he could make me another one, but at that point I didn’t want a replacement. I simply asked him to add more ice.

For a drink that costs around $8, I expect much better quality and service. I wouldn’t have even bought it if my daughter hadn’t wanted one.

The whole experience was disappointing, from
having to wait while the employee was on his phone, to the way the drink was prepared, to being told to “wait for the ice to melt” when I complained that my 100% ice drink wasn’t cold.

Management should really look into the service and drink quality at this location. Experiences like this may explain why the store was so quiet.

I really liked this apartment complex and was genuinely interested in renting a unit here. Unfortunately, my experience with the property manager, Katrina, was extremely disappointing.

I contacted her 4 days in advance and arranged a viewing appointment for 5:45 PM. On the day of the viewing, at 5:15 PM, just 30 minutes before the scheduled appointment, she called me and claimed that she had tried to reach me earlier that day and had left me a voicemail. However, I never received any voicemail from her and there was no missing call

She then informed me that the current tenant would no longer be available to show the apartment after 5:30 PM and asked if I could come before then. This gave me only 15 minutes to get there. Fortunately, my husband was able to go instead, as we live nearby

Although he was shown the apartment, several things were disappointing. The storage locker was not shown because the manager said she did not have the keys. She also promised to send me available dates for a follow-up viewing so I could see the unit myself, but three days have now passed and I have received no follow-up or any available dates

Calling someone just 15 minutes before an appointment and expecting them to rearrange their plans at the last minute is unprofessional. Claiming to have left a voicemail that was never received, failing to provide access to all the advertised facilities, and then not following up as promised only made the experience worse.

It is particularly frustrating because I genuinely like this building and would have considered renting here. However, after this experience, I have serious concerns about the quality of the management. If this is how prospective tenants are treated before they even move in, I can only imagine what communication and service might be like after signing a lease

Unfortunately, despite liking the property itself, I would think twice about renting here because of this experience with the manager

However, I believe an insurance professional should clearly explain important optional coverages and the financial consequences of declining them, especially to a customer who relies on the agent’s professional guidance.
Had this been properly explained to me, I would have seriously considered adding Collision Coverage. This experience resulted in a significant financial loss and was extremely disappointing. one_star_reviews.text:
This was our second year at OYS. We had a good enough experience the first year that I felt comfortable registering my child for a full month this summer. Unfortunately, our experience this year was very different.

During the month, there were days when the children could not sail — including one due to wildfire/air-quality conditions and another due to rain. I completely understand that weather is outside OYS’s control. My concern was how the program was managed when the children could not go out on the water.

I originally chose sailing because I thought an outdoor, active program would be a great fit for a child with ADHD. On non-sailing days, however, the children were kept in a small indoor space. In our experience, staff did not appear to have the training or experience needed to manage a child with ADHD in that setting. When behavioural difficulties arose, the response was suspension rather than working with the family on appropriate support.

I also had safety concerns based on what I personally observed. I saw children near the waterfront without life jackets and with very limited supervision nearby, and parent/guardian ID was not never checked at pickup.

Despite many rounds of communication, I never received a written incident report. I repeatedly asked for documentation and clarification about what happened and how the decisions were made, but was essentially told that there had been internal meetings and that their internal documentation was confidential.

My concerns were ultimately escalated to Director Jane Lumbers, but the decision remained unchanged. OYS also emphasized its non-profit status and ongoing operating costs when explaining why the unused portion of this paid program would not be refunded. This is not an inexpensive program. Non-profit or not, parents should reasonably expect appropriate supervision, clear documentation and accountability.

Only afterwards did I notice other Google reviews raising concerns involving Jane. I wish I had seen those reviews before registering for a full month — I would have taken them as a red flag.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend this program for children with ADHD or other additional support needs without first asking very specific questions about staff training, rainy-day/indoor arrangements, behavioural support, supervision and disciplinary procedures.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wish to share a situation that deeply concerned me and which, in my opinion, deserves the attention of the management of this residence.

I met an elderly woman near the Dollarama who asked me to help her get home. Out of respect for her privacy, I will not mention her name.
The woman was in a state that greatly worried me. Her hair was very unkempt and she was poorly dressed, her face was dirty, and she was still wearing a hospital bracelet. She explained that she had just been to the hospital for a health problem. She also told me about her Parkinson's disease. I noticed that she had great difficulty standing and walking on her own.

Yet she was alone outside with her groceries and needed to get back to her residence, located about three minutes from the Dollarama. I therefore decided to accompany her and carry her bag to ensure she got home safely. Upon arrival, I explained the situation to a staff member and expressed my concerns about the woman's condition. Unfortunately, I felt my comment wasn't taken as seriously as I thought it deserved. However, upon seeing her, I could clearly see that she was not well.

I don't claim to know all the details of her situation, but I believe that an elderly person with significant difficulty walking who has just been discharged from the hospital shouldn't have to ask strangers for help getting home.
If I were a member of this woman's family, I would be very concerned to know that she is alone outside in this condition and has to rely on strangers to ensure her safe return.
I sincerely hope that the facility's management will take this situation seriously, investigate what happened, and implement the necessary measures to ensure the safety and well-being of its residents. Elderly people deserve to be accompanied, monitored and treated with dignity and respect.

one_star_reviews.text:
0 stars if I could.

Extremely disappointing customer service experience at Luggage Outlet Argentia in Mississauga. The salesperson, Vishal, was extremely rude, dismissive, and unprofessional throughout our visit.

We spent approximately 30 minutes looking at three different pieces of luggage, which would have been over $500 in total. We were seriously considering the purchase, but wanted to make sure we understood the final price before spending that amount.

We repeatedly asked Vishal what the final price would be, and his response was, “I already told you the price.” The reason we kept asking was because there was confusion regarding a 10% employee discount that had been offered to us. His communication about the discount was unclear, which is exactly why we wanted to confirm the final price.

During the interaction, he also told us, “Make sure you guys put back the luggages where they were.” We are customers, not his employees. The way he spoke to us was completely unnecessary and disrespectful.

After he again responded that he had already told us the price, we finally said, “You know what, I’ll just buy one,” because he had already ruined the experience for us.

Then the situation became even more frustrating. Once we decided to purchase only one, Vishal said he would not give us the 10% discount and indicated that the discount was only available if we purchased all three. This was especially frustrating because the discount had previously been offered, and his communication about the conditions was not clear from the beginning.

This is exactly why we were asking questions about the final price. We were considering spending over $500, and we should have been able to get a clear answer without being treated like we were wasting his time.

After we decided to only purchase one, Vishal immediately started rushing to put the display luggage back in its place, further making us feel unwelcome.

We were in the store for approximately 30 minutes, yet he acted as though we had been there for several hours. We were customers considering a $500+ purchase—not employees and certainly not an inconvenience.

In the end, we left the store because of Vishal’s customer service. What could have been a $500+ purchase was lost because of the way we were treated.

There was also another interaction that was extremely uncomfortable to witness. Around the time we were preparing to leave, a family with two toddlers entered the showroom. Vishal told the father to put the children on the floor outside the showroom while they shopped. I found this completely inappropriate and disturbing. How can you reasonably expect a parent to leave two toddlers on the floor outside while they shop?

The father ignored the comment and brought the toddlers inside, as any parent would reasonably do. What made the situation even more uncomfortable was that the family looked over at us during the disagreement we were having with Vishal after he repeatedly said, “I already told you the price.” They appeared to witness part of the interaction themselves.

At this point, it was clear to us that the problem was not simply a misunderstanding about pricing. The overall attitude and manner of communication were extremely disappointing.

The issue wasn't simply the discount; it was the rude attitude, poor communication, and lack of basic customer service from Vishal. Vishal’s treatment of us completely ruined our shopping experience and ultimately cost the store a potential $500+ sale. I would not recommend this location based on our experience with him. Management should seriously look into how Vishal is treating customers.

For our first visit, we spent $80 for 160 coins/credits and we walked out with two large plushies (24 points) and a goose (4 points) from the machines. The more you pay, the better of a deal you get.

And I'd say what I paid was a pretty good deal, or otherwise I mean you can pay like $20 for 22 credits which isn't really worth it at all.

The machines cost between 4-7 credits (about $4-7 if you buy credits 1:1 individually) and each machine's plushies have a point value between 1-2 (excluding one machine that costs 3 credits for small, point-less prizes), and you can exchange your winnings for bigger prizes up front, like larger plushies, Pokémon cards, a Naruto figurine, and Captain America's shield, for some reason lol

There's also some gacha machines in the back where you can win Blind Box Kuromis and other small similar figurines for I think 7 credits per machine. There's a Demon Slayer gacha machine, too.

I'd definitely recommend the place but I'm just a bit bummed out someone grabbed one of the plushies I wanted to trade for just before we could ask someone for it and we had to settle for something else instead :(

I really wanted that strawberry Kuromi...
Anyway, it happens, I guess. The place can be a bit pricey, but all in all, cool place, and definitely would come again.
And the machines are extremely fair and very, very easy to win. Check it out!

Edit: the place went to utter shit within a year. there's barely anything on the shelves, they rigged their machines, their capsule sanrio figurines are scratched up and it's all christmas plushies. disappointing.
